subject: Renewal: term structure & ramp smoothing options for NimbleAI
messages:
From: Sarah Evans <sarah.evans@nimble.ai>

Cc: procurement@nimble.ai
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal incoming — 2026 term & capacity planning

Hi Karthik,

Our renewal window for NimbleAI is coming up (contract ends 2026-06-30). We9ve seen a ~35% month-over-month increase in token usage the last three months as we bolt LLM features into our search product. Given the growth, procurement asked us to explore: a term structure that smooths billing and capacity (multi-year ramp), a co-term with other ACME services, and an explicit true-up cadence.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood provide a 24-month option with an engineered ramp (commit increases over quarters) + guaranteed burst credits for Q3?
- Is there an easy way to opt out of auto-renew within a defined window (procurement prefers 60 days)?
- We9ll need SOC2 artifacts and a DocuSign flow for legal.

I attached our last three months of usage for reference. Can we schedule 30 minutes next week to run options?

Thanks,
Sarah Evans
Head of Platform, NimbleAI
[sarah.evans@nimble.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Evans <sarah.evans@nimble.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal incoming — 2026 term & capacity planning

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the heads up and the usage file 1 that helps. We9ve talked internally and can present three practical structures that balance predictability for you and capacity economics for Redwood:

1) 12-month FLEX + quarterly true-up
   - Baseline committed tokens for Q1/Q2/Q3 with quarterly true-up.
   - Burstable pool for spikes (pre-bought credits).
   - No long-term price lock; smaller discount (5% off list).

2) 24-month RAMP (recommended for growth customers)
   - Year-1: conservative commit (covers 60% of current run-rate)
   - Year-2: pre-agreed scheduled increases each quarter (ramp ladder) to align with your product launches.
   - 10% discount in Y1, 7% in Y2; one-time onboarding credit for early ramp (canary credits to cover the first 6 weeks of traffic surges).
   - Co-terming with other ACME services possible; we can align invoice cadence.

3) 36-month STAGED-COMMIT + capacity guardrail
   - Larger commitment with deeper discounts and a capped overage rate.
   - Suitable if you want to fix unit economics across multiple product lines.

On auto-renew: we can add an explicit opt-out window. Standard is 30 days; legal can extend to 60 days for enterprise customers on a case-by-case (we9ll flag it to legal if that9s required).

Next steps I propose: 30-min call Wed (5/13) to pick option + we9ll circulate a short MAP with milestones (SOW, pricing, DocuSign target). I attached an initial options summary PDF for your review.

Would Marissa and Camila be ok with me outlining the proposed MAP on the call?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

[Attachment: Renewal_Options_v1.pdf (PDF stub)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal incoming — 2026 term & capacity planning

Karthik / Camila,

Quick internal note before the call:
- Recommend pushing option 2 (24-month ramp) as primary; it9s lower inertia for Nimble and protects Redwood on forecast.
- Offer: 10% discount Y1, 7% Y2 + a 6-week canary credit pool (covers initial surge).
- Add quarterly true-up and quarterly billing to match procurement preference for predictable cash flow.
- Legal flag: if procurement insists on 60-day auto-renew opt-out we need signoff from Legal (risk of churn window).
- Ops note: include an SLA exception clause for planned capacity spikes in Q3 (they explicitly asked for guaranteed burst credits).

If Karthik wants, I9ll prepare a clean MAP doc with milestones and a short risk section for Legal.

-Marissa
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
